text:
alex: seeing a sudden jump in apiserver p95/p99 in eu-west1 at ~07:45 UTC, controller-manager reconcile queue spiking, many GPU pod creations timing out
maria: started when? any correlating leader churn in etcd?
jordan: yes, etcd shows a couple of quick leader changes and proposal latencies spiking. NAT metrics also show many ephemeral port allocations around the same time
alex: paste from etcd logs:
```
2026-03-19T07:44:57Z etcd-a raft: leader changed from 10.10.2.4 to 10.10.3.6
2026-03-19T07:45:12Z etcd-b raft: leader changed from 10.10.3.6 to 10.10.1.9
2026-03-19T07:45:50Z etcd-c raft: leader changed from 10.10.1.9 to 10.10.2.4
```
ops-bot: alert: apiserver-5xx-spike-eu-west1 generated, oncall notified
sam: looks like a thundering attach from dedicated GPU autoscaler + large image pulls -> egress spike -> SNAT port pressure. That would cause TCP conn stalls and raise etcd I/O due to control-plane egress healthchecks
lee: controller-manager keeps retrying on api failures, queue gets big quickly. We should reduce controller concurrency temporarily
maria: agree. Also need to consider short-term NAT IP pool expansion and adding guardrails to the provisioner to slow attach rate
jordan: immediate mitigations I propose:
- scale down controller-manager concurrency (reduce reconciles) and lower apiserver inflight limits
- add a short delay between node attach requests from provisioner (throttle)
- expand NAT IP pool temporarily in eu-west1
- monitor etcd leader stability and IOPS during mitigation
alex: I'm applying a canary patch to kcm flags to lower --concurrent-syncs to 5 and --leader-elect-lease-duration bump? maybe not change elections yet
lee: don't change election timeouts globally. We can tweak etcd heartbeat/election if we confirm transient I/O stalls from compaction, but that's a riskier config change
sam: for a quick safety valve we can route control-plane egress via an alternate peered path if NAT usage >75% (routing policy) — create a temporary route and health check
maria: file RFC later for egress-fallback and SNAT monitoring, but for now open a ticket to add attach rate limit to provisioner service
jordan: also add short-term alert: SNAT utilization >70% AND apiserver 5xxs -> auto-scale NAT IPs or notify oncall immediately
ops-bot: action created: kcm-canary-patch by lee; nat-ip-pool-expand by jordan; provisioner-ratecap by alex
lee: rolling canary now to staging then prod if stable. patch PR: #4521
alex: after patch apiserver p95 dropped ~35% and kcm queue length reduced by half. NAT ports still elevated but not critical
sam: agree this is tradeoff: throttling attach increases onboarding latency but stabilizes control plane and avoids expensive failovers
maria: medium-term: prefer private registry mirrors in region + pull-through caches for GPU images and per-AZ NAT pools so single NAT doesn't become a global choke point
jordan: also revisit etcd storage tuning; compaction spikes caused short iops blips on NVMe that amplified leader elections. Add more IO headroom and stagger compaction jobs across nodes
ops-bot: incident updated: mitigations applied, monitoring in watch window for 45m
alex: keeping an eye, will join postmortem if we need follow-up. Good catch everyone :thumbsup:
